title: Why is the sky blue?
subtitle: And why sunsets turn red
objectives: Explain why air makes the daytime sky look blue
Use the same idea to explain red sunsets
question: If sunlight looks white, why is the sky blue?

claims.text: Sunlight looks white but holds all the colors of the rainbow.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: The light from the Sun looks white. But it is really made up of all the colors of the rainbow.

claims.text: A prism separates white light into its colors.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: When white light shines through a prism, the light is separated into all its colors.

claims.text: Blue light waves are shorter than red light waves.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: Blue light waves are shorter than red light waves.

claims.text: Light travels in a straight line unless something reflects, bends or scatters it.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: All light travels in a straight line unless something gets in the way and does one of these things

claims.text: The gases and particles in air scatter sunlight in all directions.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: Sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere and is scattered in all directions by all the gases and particles in the air.

claims.text: Blue is scattered more than other colors because its waves are shorter.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: Blue is scattered more than other colors because it travels as shorter, smaller waves.

claims.text: That scattered blue light is why the sky usually looks blue.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: This is why we see a blue sky most of the time.

claims.text: Light from low in the sky has passed through more air than light from overhead.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: The sunlight reaching us from low in the sky has passed through even more air than the sunlight reaching us from overhead.

claims.text: Near the horizon the sky fades to a lighter blue or white.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: Closer to the horizon, the sky fades to a lighter blue or white.

claims.text: At sunset even more blue is scattered, so reds and yellows pass straight through.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: Even more of the blue light is scattered, allowing the reds and yellows to pass straight through to your eyes.

claims.text: Dust, pollution and other aerosols also scatter blue light, which can make the sky look red.
claims.source: NASA Space Place, Why Is the Sky Blue?
claims.quote: The sky appears red because small particles of dust, pollution, or other aerosols also scatter blue light, leaving more purely red and yellow light to go through the atmosphere.

misconception.right: All colors scatter. Blue scatters the most.

beats.say: Look up on a clear afternoon and the sky is blue.
Yet the light filling it comes from the Sun, and sunlight looks white.
So where does the blue come from?

show.text: If sunlight looks white, why is the sky blue?

beats.say: One idea answers it, and the same idea explains the red sunset.
Before the explanation, learn the three words it uses.
White sunlight is really a mix of every color of the rainbow.
A prism shows this by spreading white light into its colors.
Each color travels as a wave, and blue waves are shorter than red ones.

show.meaning: Length of one wave. Blue short, red long.

beats.say: Light goes straight unless something reflects it, bends it, or scatters it.

show.meaning: Send light off in many directions

pause.ask: Which color has the shorter waves?
pause.why: Blue light waves are shorter than red light waves.

beats.say: Sunlight enters the atmosphere and runs into gas molecules and tiny particles.
They knock the light off in all directions.
Blue gets scattered more than the other colors, because its waves are shorter.
So scattered blue reaches your eyes from all over the sky.

show.text: This is why we see a blue sky most of the time.

pause.ask: Light from low in the sky crosses more air than light from overhead. Predict: is the sky near the horizon a deeper blue or a paler blue?
pause.why: Near the horizon the sky fades to a lighter blue or white.

beats.say: A common slip is saying that only blue light gets scattered.
The gases and particles in air scatter sunlight in every direction.
Blue simply scatters more than the rest, so it is more, not only.
Now use the idea on a sunset.
When the Sun is low, its light crosses far more air to reach you.
Along that long path, even more of the blue is scattered away.
What is left, the reds and yellows, passes straight through to your eyes.

pause.ask: Smoke and dust add more small particles to the air. Predict what they do to a sunset, and why.
pause.answer: They can make it redder, because the particles also scatter blue light and leave more red and yellow.
pause.why: Dust, pollution and other aerosols also scatter blue light, leaving more red and yellow light.

beats.say: Here is the whole chain.
Sunlight carries every color.
Air scatters the short blue waves the most.
Overhead, that scattered blue fills the sky.
At sunset, the long path scatters the blue away, and red gets through.

recall.ask: Look away from the screen. In two or three sentences, explain why the sky is blue and why sunsets are red.
points: Air scatters short blue waves more than the other colors, so blue reaches you from all over the sky.
At sunset light crosses much more air, the blue is scattered away, and reds and yellows get through.

practice.ask: A wildfire far away fills the air with fine smoke. Predict the color of tonight's sunset and explain it with this lesson's idea.
practice.answer: Redder than usual. The smoke particles also scatter blue light, so even more blue is removed and more red and yellow light gets through.
steps: Smoke adds small particles to the air.
Those particles scatter blue light too.
With more blue removed, more red and yellow light reaches you.
